summary: Stem I buys; stem II sells. The frequent b spellings mzabn-/zab- belong to this supplied zwn family and do not justify inventing zbn or reassigning forms to zby.

Transactions code price with b-, source seller with m-, and beneficiary with l-suffixes; l-marked postposed agents in PrS are distinct from the beneficiary. The exact suffix segmentation of zwənnanne remains unresolved.

Finite Detransitive at 70/51 expresses buyability and saleability; Talay 2/16 has an affected Gospel sold by leaves. The inherited II Detransitive Infinitiv also covers ordinary active selling-purpose nominals; retain that filing without inferring a finite Detransitive event from each nominal.
The new I Infectum-wa evidence denotes habitual procurement. Cognate Infinitiv plus finite purchase contrasts with theft or other acquisition, without creating a new lexical sense.

PrS references in the entry use edition-page coordinates as well as text/verse coordinates in this input. Corresponding passages are concordance evidence, not grounds to replace every inherited page reference.
Resolve person and suffix components of zwənnanne at Hors 2/40 and 115/150, and prospective zunilan at 115/149; no new form is published from the latter alone.
At PrS 73/20 is Zabenən an Imperativ with plural object, or a reduced Infectum? The German has first-person intention; the form and speaker need checking.
Confirm h in komzabhətle at 116/51, preserving it until verified.
Should lexical seller mzabnone be retained under Part act.? It is entered provisionally with its nominal role stated, following the glossary's agent-noun practice.
Complete the truncated existing II Detransitive Infinitiv translation and reconcile PrS 125/22 versus 125/23 for the shared buy-and-sell quotation.
Capitalize the substantivized adjective Armen
rationale: Armen refers to the poor man and is a substantivized adjective. It requires a capital A. The edition has the same capitalization slip.

summary: Advice (ʕaql) is an abstract commodity in an explicitly priced sale, not a new figurative selling meaning. A ship can stand for its owner as seller.
